g.text: # Simulate a subscription merchant: customers, renewals, retries, disputes.
# Point-in-time features: nothing at or after the charge is visible.
# Baselines on a future test window, with a 120-day label gap.
model PR-AUC lift Brier ECE P@5%
wrote artifacts/baseline/report.md, calibration.png, metrics.json and models to artifacts/baseline/
# Price the decisions in dollars, with bootstrap intervals.
test window: 7,013 charges, 167 disputes; approve-all costs $2,455 per 1k charges
model PR-AUC [95% CI] saved/1k [95% CI] blocked
# A visa:13.2 dispute lands on txn_00005668. What did the model see?
txn_00005668: dispute risk 92.3% (49.9× a typical transaction at 1.8%). Raised by
odds). Lowered by email_freemail = no (×0.75 odds).
# Rules pick the strategy; the (mock) LLM writes the case note.
strategy: accept (playbook: accept, confidence: high, llm via mock)
rationale: Filed under visa:13.2 (Cancelled Recurring Transaction). Before the dispute, the
model scored this charge at 92.3%, 49.9× a typical transaction. The score was driven
by charged_after_cancel_request = yes (×1,668 odds), email_freemail = no (×0.75
odds), prior_approved_renewals = 2 (×1.27 odds). Playbook signals: the customer had
already asked to cancel before this charge; established account (279.7 days old) with
no IP/issuer country mismatch; 2 approved renewals of this subscription before the
charge. Recommended action: accept. The customer asked to cancel before this charge,
so the merchant is at fault.
- refund confirmation, or accept the chargeback without a response
# Draft the representment packet from evidence the merchant holds.
# The top of the packet: readiness, deadline and rebuttal.
| Reason code | Visa 13.2 — Cancelled Recurring Transaction |
Not drafted: an adverse fact applies (see the analyst section). Refund or accept.
